verdicts.reason: The summary says "a 2002 paper used simple compression techniques to cluster languages and infer their evolutionary relationships without prior linguistic knowledge", which paraphrases the main claim.
It says cross-entropy measures "how well a compression scheme optimized for one context performs in another", which is the core definition, though asymmetry is not mentioned.
The summary says nothing about the minimum at P equals Q, the entropy, or KL divergence.
It only says it "explains how cross-entropy loss functions in pre-training", without stating the negative log probability of the true next token or why the log is forced.
Distillation is only named in passing, with no claim that a small model is trained against a larger model's full distribution.
